case_title: RAKESH & ANR. v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that two appellants, along with another accused, caused the death of the victim by assaulting him with sharp edged weapons. The victim was taken to the hospital where he was examined by a doctor and declared dead. The accused were arrested, and the weapons used in the crime were recovered on their disclosure statements. The trial court convicted the two appellants under Section 302 IPC and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for life. The conviction was upheld by the High Court. The appellants challenged their conviction on the grounds that the ocular evidence was contradictory to the medical evidence regarding the time of death and that the alleged eye witness was closely related to the victim. The Supreme Court held that the ocular evidence had primacy unless it was established that oral evidence was totally irreconcilable with the medical evidence. The Court also noted that the witness's testimony was trustworthy and that the prosecution case was supported by other evidence, including the statements of the Investigating Officer and the recovery of weapons.
